Emma / Harrison — thanks for the redlines and the subprocessor list. I've reviewed with Product and Legal; below is our working position to speed to a consolidated redline.

Summary of Redwood position (draft):
- Controller / Processor: we can accept the narrower controller obligations for Cordelia, but we cannot take broad indemnity for third-party subprocessors. We propose replacing a broad indemnity with a capped liability tied to order form value for subprocessor-caused breaches and carve an obligation to use commercially reasonable efforts to require subprocessors to comply.
- SCCs & Transfer Addendum: we will adopt the 2021 SCCs and are open to a transfer-addendum that provides an execution pathway if a local ruling restricts transfers. Proposed language: we will offer either VPC-region pinning or, as fallback, an order-form-scoped transfer-addendum to be applied per-region.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS for tenant isolation is possible on Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments only. Hosted standard customers (shared pool) cannot have key export capability. If Cordelia requires customer-managed KMS, that should be scoped to the Dedicated or Private line item on the order form and priced accordingly.
- Subprocessor evidence: we can provide a SOC2 summary package and commit to quarterly updates to the subprocessor roster; we cannot provide full audit access to Redwood production environments but can provide evidence artifacts (SOC2 AICPA report) and a contract provision for on-site audits with advance notice and mutual NDA — rare but possible for enterprise with a separate engagement.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Ben to surface pricing delta for KMS / Dedicated requirement and a ballpark timeline for Dedicated onboarding.
2) Legal (Irene / Laura) to produce a markup that replaces broad subprocessor indemnity with a capped/liability-based approach and formalizes the transfer-addendum language.
3) Schedule a 30-minute call with Cordelia + Redwood Legal + Sales (tomorrow or Wednesday next week) to walk the consolidated redline.

I've uploaded a working consolidation draft to the shared doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xYz-doc-dpa-consolidation — please review and add comments by EOD Monday so we can circulate a signature-ready version.

Diego

Subject: Final legal position & request for confirmation

Emma / Harrison — following internal review we've produced the consolidated legal markup (see the shared doc and inline comments). Key points for Cordelia to confirm so we can finalise:

1) Subprocessor liability: Redwood will accept removal of a broad unlimited indemnity clause. In place we will accept a limited-liability approach tied to the value of the order form (cap = 12 months' fees for the order form line items) and a requirement to demonstrate that any claim arose from Redwood's failure to comply with the DPA (i.e., not third-party negligence outside our control).

2) Audit & evidence: we will provide SOC2 Type II summary artifacts and a packaged evidence deliverable for subprocessors. If Cordelia needs additional on-site or forensic access, that should be handled under a separate statement of work and may carry a professional services fee.

3) KMS / Hosting: customer-managed KMS can be delivered, but only on Dedicated or Private. We need Cordelia to indicate in the order form which option they select. If Cordelia selects Hosted + customer-controlled restrictions (but not KMS), we will provide region pinning and contractual export-path constraints; we cannot offer key export for shared hosted nodes.

4) Transfer addendum: we will include an Annex for transfer-addendum protocols — we propose an operational playbook that sits as a Schedule to the DPA describing technical routing, notification cadence, and a fall-back region policy. Please confirm any required changes to the playbook within 5 business days.

Next operational asks:
- Emma: confirm which deployment class Cordelia prefers (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and whether the KMS requirement is mandatory.
- Harrison: if Cordelia is comfortable with the capped-liability substitute language, please mark approval in the shared doc; once approved we'll produce a clean redline for signature.
- Cordelia procurement/legal: if approved, we'll send the DocuSign envelope (https://www.docusign.net/cordelia/CDEL-2026-048).

If there's no objection, legal will issue the signature-ready DPA and updated order-form exhibits by EOD Wednesday. If the KMS + Dedicated pricing is accepted, Ben will send a formal amendment for the order form by Tuesday.
